## gods-eye-view-data__README.md
# God's Eye View bundled datasets

Static geospatial datasets mirrored from the [God's Eye View](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view)
project (`src/data/local_data/`), republished here so applications can stream them
instead of vendoring several megabytes of GeoJSON into every build.

Published by [opengeos](https://github.com/opengeos) for use by
[GeoLibre](https://github.com/opengeos/GeoLibre). Tracking issue:
[opengeos/GeoLibre#2462](https://github.com/opengeos/GeoLibre/issues/2462).

**Licensing is per directory and not uniform.** Two directories are not openly
licensed. Read [LICENSE](LICENSE) before using or redistributing anything here.

## Contents

| Directory | Files | Features | License |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `datacenters/` | `datacenters.geojsonl` (2.4 MB) | 4,351 | ODbL 1.0 |
| `dams/` | `dams.geojson`, `dams.geojsonl` (713 KB each) | 704 | ODbL 1.0 |
| `natural_earth/` | `regions.json` (1.9 MB), `marine.json` (619 KB) | 1,046 / 292 | Public domain |
| `neighborhoods/` | `san-francisco.json` (217 KB) | 41 | PDDL 1.0 (public domain) |
| `telegeography_submarine_cables/` | `cable-geo.json` (711 KB), `landing-point-geo.json` (351 KB) | 712 cables, 1,917 landing points | **CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (NonCommercial)** |
| `cctv_ground_heights/` | `cctv_ground_heights.json` (1.9 MB) | 3,445 cameras | **Not stated upstream, see LICENSE** |

Every directory keeps the original upstream `README.md` (or `SOURCE.md`) describing
provenance, extraction filters, and transforms. `DATA_SOURCES.md` at the root is the
upstream project-wide attribution and licensing summary.

## Access

Objects are served directly over HTTPS:

```
https://data.source.coop/opengeos/geolibre/gods-eye-view-data/<path>
```

For example:

```bash
curl -O https://data.source.coop/opengeos/geolibre/gods-eye-view-data/dams/dams.geojson
```

## Dataset notes

### datacenters/

OpenStreetMap-derived datacenter features. The public snapshot removes
contact-oriented tags (email, phone, fax, mobile, WhatsApp); the remaining fields are
feature identity, geometry, name, operator, and capacity metadata.

Upstream records that the original extraction date and Overpass query were **not**
captured for this snapshot. Treat it as an undated extract. A future refresh should
record both.

### dams/

Extracted from decoded [Open Infrastructure Map](https://openinframap.org/) PostGIS
layers, filtered on `waterway=dam`, `man_made=dam`, or `building=dam`. The same
contact-field privacy transform is applied. `dams.geojson` and `dams.geojsonl` carry
identical content in FeatureCollection and line-delimited form.

### natural_earth/

Named physical and marine region polygons from Natural Earth 10m physical vectors
(`ne_10m_geography_regions_polys`, `ne_10m_geography_marine_polys`), via
[nvkelso/natural-earth-vector](https://github.com/nvkelso/natural-earth-vector) at commit
`ca96624a56bd078437bca8184e78163e5039ad19`. Curated upstream: named features only, outer
rings only, Douglas-Peucker simplified at 0.01 degrees, coordinates rounded to 3 decimals.
Drake Passage and Luzon Strait are absent because they exist only as sliver artifacts in
the source.

### neighborhoods/

San Francisco Analysis Neighborhoods from DataSF (dataset `j2bu-swwd`), retrieved
2026-07-30. Simplified with a 2e-5 degree tolerance and rounded to 6 decimals. Names are
kept verbatim from the `nhood` column.

### telegeography_submarine_cables/

Submarine cable routes and landing points from TeleGeography's
[Submarine Cable Map](https://www.submarinecablemap.com/), downloaded 2026-05-24.

**This directory is NonCommercial and is not open data.** See [LICENSE](LICENSE).
Applications are encouraged to fetch this data live from TeleGeography's public
endpoints rather than depend on this copy:

- `https://www.submarinecablemap.com/api/v3/cable/cable-geo.json`
- `https://www.submarinecablemap.com/api/v3/landing-point/landing-point-geo.json`

`source.json` records sha256 checksums for both files, so a mirrored copy can be verified
against the upstream capture.

### cctv_ground_heights/

Precomputed ground heights under CCTV camera positions and their monitor-plane support
points, in WGS84 ellipsoidal metres, generated by sampling Google Photorealistic 3D Tiles.

**Upstream states no license for this dataset**, and the upstream `DATA_SOURCES.md`
separately notes that Google Maps Content may not be cached, stored, rehosted, or
committed. Whether these derived height measurements fall under that restriction is
unresolved. See [LICENSE](LICENSE) before using or redistributing this directory.

## Attribution

Applications consuming the ODbL datasets must display:

```
© OpenStreetMap contributors
```

with a link to https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright, plus an Open Infrastructure Map
credit for `dams/`. Natural Earth requires no attribution but a "Made with Natural Earth"
credit is customary. See [LICENSE](LICENSE) for the full set of required notices.


## gods-eye-view-data__cctv_ground_heights__README.md
# CCTV ground heights

Precomputed ground height under every camera in the served CCTV catalog and
under the nine support points of its monitor plane, aligned to work with
Google Photorealistic 3D Tiles. Heights are WGS84 ellipsoidal metres. The
client places a camera and its plane from this file with no runtime sampling.

Runtime output: `cctv_ground_heights.json`

```
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "provider": "google-3d-tiles",
  "heightReference": "WGS84-ellipsoid",
  "generatedAt": "<ISO>",
  "cameras": {
    "<camera id>": {
      "poseHash": "p1-…",          // hash of the served pose the entry describes
      "status": "ok" | "miss",
      "mountGroundM": <number>,    // ground under the camera position (absent on a miss)
      "supports": {                // ground under the plane's 3×3 support grid; null where
        "bl","bm","br",            // a point has no value (absent on a miss)
        "ml","mc","mr",
        "tl","tm","tr"
      },
      "misses": [<keys with no value>],
      "sampledAt": "<ISO>",
      "attempts": <n>
    }
  }
}
```

Support point positions are defined by `src/data/cctvFootprint.js`
(`planeSupportPoints`), shared with the server join
(`server/providers/cctv/groundHeights.js`). An entry is used only while the
camera's served pose still hashes to `poseHash`; a camera whose feed moved it,
or whose pose a user edited, falls back to runtime placement from the terrain
proxy.

Regenerate against a running app (resumable; only cameras whose pose changed
or whose entry is incomplete are redone):

```
GEV_BASE=http://localhost:4173 node scripts/precompute-cctv-heights.mjs
```


## gods-eye-view-data__dams__README.md
# Dams

Extracted from local decoded OpenInfraMap/PostGIS layers.

Filters: `waterway=dam`, `man_made=dam`, or `building=dam`.

Feature count: 704

Runtime output: `dams.geojsonl`

License: Open Database License (ODbL) 1.0. Keep the OpenStreetMap contributor
attribution and the Open Infrastructure Map source credit when redistributing
this derived database.

The public-release snapshot removes contact-oriented fields and note values
that contain email or phone identifiers. The runtime layer does not display or
depend on those fields. Both `dams.geojson` and the runtime JSONL form carry the
same privacy transform.


## gods-eye-view-data__datacenters__README.md
# Datacenters

OpenStreetMap-derived datacenter features bundled for the local infrastructure
layer.

- Source: OpenStreetMap contributors
- License: Open Database License (ODbL) 1.0
- Feature count: 4,351
- Runtime file: `datacenters.geojsonl`

The public-release snapshot removes contact-oriented tags such as email, phone,
fax, mobile, and WhatsApp values. The application does not display or depend on
those fields; it uses feature identity, geometry, name, operator, and capacity
metadata. The remaining derived database continues to be distributed under
ODbL 1.0 with the required OpenStreetMap attribution.

The original extraction date and query were not recorded alongside this
snapshot. Future refreshes should record both before replacing the file.


## gods-eye-view-data__natural_earth__README.md
# Natural Earth physical regions pack

Offline named-region polygons for the voice-annotation resolver
(`src/data/naturalEarthRegions.js`) — "outline the Alps" resolves to the real
range geometry with no network dependency.

| File | Source dataset | Features |
|------|----------------|----------|
| `regions.json` | `ne_10m_geography_regions_polys` (ranges, deserts, plateaus, peninsulas, islands, …) | 1,046 named |
| `marine.json` | `ne_10m_geography_marine_polys` (seas, gulfs, straits, bays, …) | 292 named |

**Source:** Natural Earth 10m physical vectors, via the canonical
[nvkelso/natural-earth-vector](https://github.com/nvkelso/natural-earth-vector)
GitHub repo, commit `ca96624a56bd078437bca8184e78163e5039ad19` (fetched
2026-07-28T01:36:39Z — exact provenance is in each file's `meta` header).

**License:** public domain (https://www.naturalearthdata.com/about/terms-of-use/).
No attribution legally required; we credit "Made with Natural Earth" anyway.
See DATA_SOURCES.md.

**Curation** (script not committed — parameters recorded in `meta.curation`):

- Named features only; the `Dragons-be-here` joke feature ("Null Island") dropped.
- Outer rings only (holes are irrelevant at country-scale outline zoom).
- Douglas-Peucker simplification at 0.01°, coordinates rounded to 3 decimals
  (~110 m), rings stored open (no closing duplicate vertex).
- MultiPolygon crumbs under 20 km² dropped (largest part always kept);
  rings that survive with fewer than 8 distinct vertices are midpoint-densified
  (shape-identical) so every ring has ≥8 vertices.
- Zero-area sliver artifacts dropped. Two marine features are ONLY slivers in
  the source and are therefore absent: **Drake Passage** and **Luzon Strait**.
- Result: 7.3 MB source → 2.5 MB pack (budget ≤3 MB, enforced by
  `src/data/naturalEarthRegions.test.mjs`).

Duplicate names exist upstream (two "Cordillera Oriental", a sliver + real
"Canadian Shield", …); the lookup module resolves ties by largest area.


## gods-eye-view-data__telegeography_submarine_cables__README.md
# TeleGeography Submarine Cable Map

Bundled GeoJSON for international submarine cable systems and landing points,
from TeleGeography's [Submarine Cable Map](https://www.submarinecablemap.com/).

## ⚠️ License — NOT covered by this project's MIT license

This dataset is licensed by TeleGeography under
**Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 (CC BY-NC-SA 3.0)**.
It is bundled here for an out-of-the-box experience and is **excluded from the
MIT license that covers God's Eye View's source code.**

- **Attribution required:** "© TeleGeography — submarinecablemap.com"
- **NonCommercial:** the data may not be used commercially. If you use this
  project commercially, **remove these files** (`cable-geo.json`,
  `landing-point-geo.json`) or obtain a commercial license from TeleGeography.
- **ShareAlike:** redistributed/adapted copies of the data must stay under
  CC BY-NC-SA 3.0.

The richer structured dataset is licensed separately/commercially by
TeleGeography. See [`DATA_SOURCES.md`](../../../../DATA_SOURCES.md) for the
project-wide data-licensing summary.

## Files

| File | Source URL | Features |
|---|---|---|
| `cable-geo.json` | `https://www.submarinecablemap.com/api/v3/cable/cable-geo.json` | 712 cables |
| `landing-point-geo.json` | `https://www.submarinecablemap.com/api/v3/landing-point/landing-point-geo.json` | 1,917 landing points |

Downloaded 2026-05-24. Re-fetch from the source URLs above to update.


## landxml-samples__README.md
# GeoLibre LandXML sample datasets

These synthetic datasets are ready to upload to the `giswqs/opengeos` Source
Cooperative repository. Keep the filenames unchanged because GeoLibre's sample
menu uses the resulting URLs.

| File | Coordinate system | Contents |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `landxml-boston-site-wgs84.xml` | EPSG:4326 | Existing-ground TIN, site access alignment, vertical profile, and control points |
| `landxml-minneapolis-road-utm15n.xml` | EPSG:26915 | Road-corridor TIN, line/curve/spiral alignment, vertical profile, and survey monuments |
| `landxml-london-earthworks-bng.xml` | EPSG:27700 | Existing and proposed TIN surfaces plus setting-out points |

Expected public URLs after upload:

- `https://data.source.coop/giswqs/opengeos/landxml-boston-site-wgs84.xml`
- `https://data.source.coop/giswqs/opengeos/landxml-minneapolis-road-utm15n.xml`
- `https://data.source.coop/giswqs/opengeos/landxml-london-earthworks-bng.xml`

The files were created for GeoLibre and dedicated to the public domain under
CC0 1.0. Their coordinates and project names are synthetic and are intended
only for software testing and demonstration.


## spaceborne-lidar__README.md
# Spaceborne LiDAR sample granules (ICESat-2 and GEDI)

Real NASA granules used to develop and test GeoLibre's **Add Data → ICESat-2 /
GEDI** reader (issue opengeos/GeoLibre#3078, PR opengeos/GeoLibre#3079). All
five are HDF5 files, downloaded on 2026-10-09 with Earthdata Login credentials
from `~/.netrc`. Each one crosses the eastern United States, including East
Tennessee (about 83.75°W, 36.0°N).

## Files

| File | Product | Archive | Size |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ATL06_20230629230240_01492006_007_01.h5` | ICESat-2 ATL06 Land Ice Height, v007 | NSIDC | 56 MB |
| `ATL08_20230629230240_01492006_007_01.h5` | ICESat-2 ATL08 Land and Vegetation Height, v007 | NSIDC | 56 MB |
| `GEDI02_A_2022158224411_O19743_03_T10532_02_004_02_V003.h5` | GEDI L2A Elevation and Height Metrics, v003 | LP DAAC | 1.6 GB |
| `GEDI02_B_2022158224411_O19743_03_T10532_02_003_01_V002.h5` | GEDI L2B Canopy Cover and Vertical Profile Metrics, v002 | LP DAAC | 447 MB |
| `GEDI04_A_2022158224411_O19743_03_T10532_02_003_01_V002.h5` | GEDI L4A Aboveground Biomass Density, v2.1 | ORNL DAAC | 300 MB |

### ICESat-2 (ATL06, ATL08)

- Acquired on 2023-06-29 between about 23:02 and 23:10 UTC, on reference
  ground track 0149. The track runs from Hudson Bay (about 59.5°N, 80.3°W) to
  northern Florida (about 29.3°N, 84.5°W).
- There are six beams, `gt1l` to `gt3r`, in three pairs. In this granule the
  `l` beam of each pair is strong and the `r` beam is weak.
- ATL06 has 40,463 land-ice segments on `gt1l`, and 235,374 segments across
  all beams. 143,202 of them pass `atl06_quality_summary == 0`.
- ATL08 has 32,371 land segments across all beams. Every segment has a valid
  `h_te_best_fit`.
- Useful fields:
  - ATL06: `land_ice_segments/h_li` and `h_li_sigma`.
  - ATL08: `land_segments/terrain/h_te_best_fit`,
    `land_segments/canopy/h_canopy`, `canopy_openness`, `night_flag` and
    `segment_landcover`.
- `delta_time` counts seconds since 2018-01-01T00:00:00Z. Float fill values
  are 3.4028235e+38.

### GEDI (L2A, L2B, L4A)

- All three come from orbit O19743 on 2022-06-07 (day 158), between about
  23:32 and 23:42 UTC. The orbit runs from British Columbia (about 51°N,
  122°W) across the US to the Guianas.
- There are eight beams. `BEAM0000`, `BEAM0001`, `BEAM0010` and `BEAM0011`
  are coverage beams. `BEAM0101`, `BEAM0110`, `BEAM1000` and `BEAM1011` are
  full-power beams. Each beam holds about 167,000 shots, about 1.34 million
  in total.
- The quality flags are:
  - L2A: `l2a_quality_flag_rel3`. Version 003 renamed it from
    `quality_flag`. 332,222 shots pass.
  - L2B: `l2b_quality_flag`. 275,595 shots pass.
  - L4A: `l4_quality_flag`. 106,557 shots pass.
- Useful fields:
  - L2A: `elev_lowestmode`, `rh` (a 2-D array of shots × 101 percentiles,
    where `rh[:, 98]` is rh98), and `sensitivity`.
  - L2B: `cover`, `pai`, `fhd_normal`, and `rh100` (stored in centimeters).
  - L4A: `agbd`, `agbd_se`, and `sensitivity`.
- L2B keeps its coordinates under `geolocation/`. L2A and L4A keep them at
  the beam root, as `lat_lowestmode` and `lon_lowestmode`.
- GEDI uses -9999 (and -999999 for `digital_elevation_model`) as fill values,
  often without declaring `_FillValue`.
- Over East Tennessee this summer pass is mostly cloud-affected. In a view of
  about 85.08–82.42°W, 35.14–36.85°N, 31,487 shots fall inside the view, but
  0 pass the L4A quality flag and 1 passes the L2B flag. Turn the quality
  filter off to see the track there.

## Loading in GeoLibre

1. Open **Add Data → ICESat-2 / GEDI** (in the 3D layers section, or search
   the command palette for "ICESat-2").
2. Choose one of these files. The product is detected from its `short_name`
   attribute.
3. Pick the beams and fields, and optionally:
   - apply the quality filter;
   - limit the read to the current map view;
   - cap the number of points.
4. Click **Add layer**.

Each footprint also gets `beam`, `beam_type`, `time` (UTC) and `distance_km`.
To draw an along-track profile, open the layer's attribute table, choose
**Charts → Scatter**, and plot `distance_km` against a height field.

## Re-downloading

The files need an Earthdata Login (https://urs.earthdata.nasa.gov) entry in
`~/.netrc`:

```bash
curl -sSfL --netrc -c cookies.txt -b cookies.txt -O <url>
```

| File | URL |
| --- | --- |
| ATL06 | https://data.nsidc.earthdatacloud.nasa.gov/nsidc-cumulus-prod-protected/ATLAS/ATL06/007/2023/06/29/ATL06_20230629230240_01492006_007_01.h5 |
| ATL08 | https://data.nsidc.earthdatacloud.nasa.gov/nsidc-cumulus-prod-protected/ATLAS/ATL08/007/2023/06/29/ATL08_20230629230240_01492006_007_01.h5 |
| GEDI L2A | https://data.lpdaac.earthdatacloud.nasa.gov/lp-prod-protected/GEDI02_A.003/GEDI02_A_2022158224411_O19743_03_T10532_02_004_02_V003/GEDI02_A_2022158224411_O19743_03_T10532_02_004_02_V003.h5 |
| GEDI L2B | https://data.lpdaac.earthdatacloud.nasa.gov/lp-prod-protected/GEDI02_B.002/GEDI02_B_2022158224411_O19743_03_T10532_02_003_01_V002/GEDI02_B_2022158224411_O19743_03_T10532_02_003_01_V002.h5 |
| GEDI L4A | https://data.ornldaac.earthdata.nasa.gov/protected/gedi/GEDI_L4A_AGB_Density_V2_1/data/GEDI04_A_2022158224411_O19743_03_T10532_02_003_01_V002.h5 |

To find other granules, query NASA's public CMR search API. For example,
these are ATL08 granules over a bounding box:

```text
https://cmr.earthdata.nasa.gov/search/granules.json?short_name=ATL08&bounding_box=-84.0,35.5,-83.5,36.0&temporal=2023-06-01T00:00:00Z,2023-08-31T00:00:00Z
```

The short names are `ATL06`, `ATL08`, `GEDI02_A`, `GEDI02_B` and
`GEDI_L4A_AGB_Density_V2_1_2056`. GEDI collected no data from March 2023 to
April 2024, while the instrument was in storage.
